K2 is the world's second-highest mountain at twenty-eight thousand two hundred fifty-one feet, located in the Karakoram Range on the Pakistan-China border. It is considered more technically difficult and dangerous than Everest, and climbers refer to it as the Savage Mountain due to its punishing conditions and high fatality rate of roughly one death for every four summits. Known locally as Chogori in Balti, the name K2 derives from being the second peak in the Karakoram. Italian climbers Ardito Desio and Marcello Lacedelli made the first ascent in nineteen fifty-four as part of an Italian expedition. Summer attempts are concentrated in a narrow window from July through August when crevasses are visible and weather is marginally more stable. The Savage Mountain epithet reflects its extreme technical difficulty, unpredictable weather, and avalanche danger. Notable ascents include Wanda Rutkiewicz reaching the peak in nineteen eighty-six, becoming the first woman to summit K2, and speed climbs becoming more common in recent decades. The mountain claims many lives each year, with two thousand eight seeing a particularly deadly climbing season with over twenty deaths.
